overview.mechanism: S-adenosylmethionine participates in cellular methylation and pathways involved in glutathione synthesis.
uses: Studied for symptomatic and biochemical improvement in intrahepatic cholestasis; indications differ by product and route.

paragraphs.text: A systematic review included three randomized and six nonrandomized studies and reported improvements in some liver enzymes and symptoms. Heterogeneous designs and short follow-up limit conclusions about disease progression or survival.

An older placebo-controlled trial in 220 patients with chronic liver disease reported short-term improvement in cholestasis measures. These findings do not establish a renal-protective effect or a kidney dosing schedule.

sources.citation: Early treatment efficacy of S-adenosylmethionine in patients with intrahepatic cholestasis: A systematic review. PubMed PMID: 32184941.
Frezza et al. Oral S-adenosylmethionine in the symptomatic treatment of intrahepatic cholestasis. A double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Gastroenterology. 1990;99:211–215. PubMed PMID: 2188871.

revision_log.change: Source-linked descriptive overview and clinical evidence; no new unsupported dose recommendation or inferred dialysis schedule.
